drivingQuestion: If one roasted an egg against the mishna's prohibition, what is the ruling?
outcomeNote: Rav Yosef's ruling proven from the mishna

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: גִּלְגֵּל מַאי? אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: גִּלְגֵּל — חַיָּיב חַטָּאת. אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: One who violated the halakha in the mishna and «slightly roasted» an egg next to an urn, «what is» the ruling? «Rav Yosef said: One» who «slightly cooked» an egg is «liable to» bring «a sin-offering,» as he performed the act of cooking on Shabbat, which is prohibited by Torah law. «Mar, son of Ravina, said: We also learned» something similar in the mishna:

segments.he: כׇּל שֶׁבָּא בְּחַמִּין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת — שׁוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּחַמִּין בְּשַׁבָּת, וְכׇל שֶׁלֹּא בָּא בְּחַמִּין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשַּׁבָּת — מְדִיחִין אוֹתוֹ בְּחַמִּין בַּשַּׁבָּת. חוּץ מִן הַמָּלִיחַ יָשָׁן וְקוֹלְיָיס הָאִיסְפָּנִין, שֶׁהַדָּחָתָן זוֹ הִיא גְּמַר מְלַאכְתָּן. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «Any» salted food item «that was» already «placed in hot water,» i.e., cooked, «before Shabbat, one may soak it in hot water» even «on Shabbat. And anything that was not placed in hot water before Shabbat, one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat,» but may not soak it, «with the exception of old salted» fish or the «colias of the Spaniards [kolyas ha’ispanin]» fish, «for which rinsing» with hot water «itself is completion of the prohibited labor» of cooking. Once it is rinsed in hot water, it does not require any additional cooking. The same is true with regard to an egg that was slightly cooked. Since it thereby becomes edible, one who brought it to that state has violated the prohibition of cooking. The Gemara sums up: Indeed, «conclude from it» that this is its meaning.
